27-insurance-4-layers: Your car insurance changes from December fifteenth. Here's what to tick.
Every policy now comes in four sections, and you get an option form to choose them.
Third party is mandatory. So is personal accident cover for you, the owner driver.
Own damage, cover for passengers, and accident cover for other occupants are optional.
For a newer car, don't skip own damage. And check the premium for each section in the schedule.

28-fastag-local-pass: Live near a toll plaza? There's a new FASTag pass for you.
If you live within twenty kilometres of a highway toll plaza, you can buy a local annual pass for that one plaza.
It's fifteen hundred rupees a year if the plaza is outside city limits, and three thousand if it's inside.
That beats paying three hundred and sixty rupees every month, if you cross that plaza through the year.
It works only at that one plaza. For long trips, the national annual pass is a different product.

29-december-or-january: Buying a car? December or January?
December has the biggest year-end discounts, and dealers want to clear old stock.
But a December build is a year older on paper, and that can lower your resale value later.
Check the manufacturing date before you pay. It's on the VIN plate and in the documents.
Keeping the car for many years? Take the December discount. Selling in two or three years? A January build is safer.

30-fog-driving: Driving in fog? Most people use the wrong lights.
High beam makes it worse. The light bounces back off the fog and blinds you.
Use low beam, and fog lamps if your car has them.
Don't drive with hazard lights on. Others can't tell if you're moving or stopped. Use them only when you've stopped.
Slow down, keep a big gap, and follow the left edge line, not the tail lights in front.
Save this for your next foggy morning.
31-cold-mornings: Winter mornings are hard on your car. Here's why.
Cold slows the chemistry inside your battery, so it has less power just when the engine needs more to start.
Tyre pressure drops in the cold too, so check it in the morning before you drive.
And engine oil is thicker when cold. Start the car, then drive gently for the first few minutes.
No need for long idling. Gentle driving warms it up faster.

32-unpaid-challan: Ignoring that traffic challan? It can come back to bite you.
Under Delhi's new traffic rules, you get forty-five days to pay or contest a challan.
Ignore it, and the offence is treated as accepted.
Pending challans can then block services like licence renewal and RC transfer.
Check your challans online with your vehicle number, and pay or contest them in time.

33-heater-vs-ac: In winter, does the heater cost you mileage?
Almost not. The heater uses hot coolant from the engine, so it's heat your engine already makes.
The fan uses a little power, but there's no compressor running.
The AC button is different. It runs the compressor, and that uses fuel.
So for warmth, use the heater with the AC off. Turn the AC on only to clear a foggy windscreen.
